sentences.en: So I'm going to begin this episode with a question.
sentences.zh: 所以，我打算用一个问题来开启本期节目。

sentences.en: When was the last time you were fully, truly alone for longer than 12 hours?
sentences.zh: 你上一次真正、完全独自一人超过12小时是什么时候？

sentences.en: When was the last time you spent a whole weekend by yourself?
sentences.zh: 你上一次独自度过整个周末是什么时候？

sentences.en: A whole day by yourself even?
sentences.zh: 甚至哪怕是独自过完整整一天？

sentences.en: And more specifically, when was the last time you did that and enjoyed yourself?
sentences.zh: 更具体地说，你上一次这么做并且乐在其中是什么时候？

sentences.en: Our relationship to loneliness but more specifically just being by ourselves, just being alone, maybe not lonely but alone impacts our 20s in ways that you cannot imagine
sentences.zh: 我们与孤独的关系，更具体地说，就是独自相处、仅仅是独处的状态——也许并非感到凄凉，但确实是孤身一人——对我们二十岁生活的影响超乎你的想象，

sentences.en: or maybe you can.
sentences.zh: 或者也许你也能想象得到。

sentences.en: It influences the partner we choose, it influences the friendships that we keep naturally of course but also the jobs we refuse to leave, the cities we never move to,
sentences.zh: 它影响我们选择的伴侣，自然而然地影响我们维持的友谊，还有我们拒绝辞去的绝不放手的工作、我们从未搬去的城市、

sentences.en: the dreams we never pursue because they might require us to spend some time by ourselves.
sentences.zh: 那些我们从未去追寻的梦想，因为这些可能都需要我们花点时间独自面对。

sentences.en: Sometimes our biggest decisions, without us even realising it, aren't driven by what we truly want but by what will prevent us from feeling lonely or being alone.
sentences.zh: 有时我们最大的决定，在甚至没有意识到的情况下，并非由我们真正想要什么来驱动，而是由什么能阻止我们感到孤独或保持独处来驱动。

sentences.en: It might seem funny, it's kind of ironic even to say that we have a relationship with loneliness but we do, every single one of us.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能有点好笑，甚至有点讽刺，去说我们与孤独之间存在着某种关系，但我们的确如此，我们每一个人都是。

sentences.en: There are some people who jump for joy at the thought of uninterrupted time by themselves all weekend, all week, they could do it forever
sentences.zh: 有些人一想到整个周末、整整一周都能有不被打扰的独处时间就会欢欣雀跃，他们觉得这样过一辈子都行，

sentences.en: but if you're like me or the average person, I think solitude feels less like a blessing, more like a second best option at best, a punishment at worSt.
sentences.zh: 但如果你和我或普通人一样，我认为独处感觉更像是一种次优选择，往好听了说是退而求其次，往难听了说简直就像是一种惩罚。

sentences.en: Today though, I want to talk about how we can get over that and how we can truly transform our relationship with loneliness to not just be something that we tolerate
sentences.zh: 不过今天，我想聊聊我们如何克服这种心理，如何真正改变我们与孤独的关系，让它不再仅仅是我们勉强容忍的事物，

sentences.en: but something we deeply enjoy, perhaps even benefit from in its entirety.
sentences.zh: 而是成为我们深切享受、甚至能全面从中受益的事物。

sentences.en: I also want to talk specifically about what you will gain from loneliness or from solitude and some very practical ways to get there because if you can choose your reaction
sentences.zh: 我还想具体谈谈你能从孤独或独处中获得什么，以及达到这一状态的一些非常实用的方法，因为如果你能自主选择自己对

sentences.en: to solitude, to isolation, to being alone, you gain a psychological power and a psychological flexibility that very few people have, especially in this day and age
sentences.zh: 独处、孤立、单处状态的反应，你就会获得一种极少数人拥有的心理力量和心理灵活性，尤其是在当今这个时代——

sentences.en: where everyone is connected to each other at literally every hour, every minute of every day.
sentences.zh: 在这个时代，每个人在一天中的每一个小时、每一分钟， literalmente（字面上）都与他人紧密相连。

sentences.en: So without further ado,
sentences.zh: 所以，废话不多说，

sentences.en: I'm very excited for this episode.
sentences.zh: 我非常期待这一期的节目。

sentences.en: Let's get into the psychology behind how you can get better at being alone.
sentences.zh: 让我们深入探讨如何更好地享受独处的心理学原理。

sentences.en: So to begin, why does feeling alone feel so just like icky and feel so weird?
sentences.zh: 那么首先，为什么感到孤独会让人感觉那么令人反感又那么怪异？

sentences.en: Why do we at times feel like we need to run away from any instance of solitude or alone time or isolation?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们有时会觉得需要逃避任何独处、单处或被隔离的时刻？

sentences.en: Let us do the simplest explanation first and one that you've likely heard quite a few times from me.
sentences.zh: 让我们先从最简单的解释说起，这也是你可能从我这里听过好几次的解释。

sentences.en: Being alone goes against deep survival instincts to stay with the herd.
sentences.zh: 独自一人违背了留在群体中的深度生存本能。

sentences.en: Those survival instincts influence us unconsciously to always gravitate back towards the group, back towards being around people.
sentences.zh: 这些生存本能无意识地影响着我们，让我们总是倾向于回归群体，回归有人的环境。

sentences.en: Some people even have such an intense instinct towards others or such an intense fear of being alone that it can develop into a phobia.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至对他人有着极其强烈的本能依恋，或者对独处有着极度恐惧，以至于发展成了某种恐惧症。

sentences.en: It's called autophobia or monophobia.
sentences.zh: 这被称为离群恐惧症或广场恐惧症（注：此处原文为autophobia或monophobia，即恐独症）。

sentences.en: This creates intense anxiety, intense panic about being by ourselves or intense fear around not being around other people.
sentences.zh: 这会产生强烈的焦虑，对独自一人感到极度恐慌，或者对身边没有其他人产生强烈的恐惧。

sentences.en: That's the first explanation, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是第一种解释。

sentences.en: And I know I mentioned the evolutionary explanation for loneliness quite a bit, but the older I get, the more I'm kind of leaning away from this theory.
sentences.zh: 我知道我经常提到关于孤独的进化论解释，但随着我年龄的增长，我越来越倾向于背离这种理论。

sentences.en: I think this idea that like we only hate loneliness because it goes against survival instincts is a little bit outdated.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种认为“我们讨厌孤独只是因为它违背了生存本能”的观点有点过时了。

sentences.en: It doesn't really consider the role of introversion.
sentences.zh: 它并没有真正考虑到内向性格的作用。

sentences.en: It doesn't really consider why some people actually like being by themselves.
sentences.zh: 它也没有真正解释为什么有些人实际上就是喜欢独自一人。

sentences.en: It doesn't explain why loneliness persists even when we are constantly around people physically, especially, you know, nowadays considering the availability of smartphones
sentences.zh: 它无法解释为什么即使我们在物理上经常被人群包围，孤独感依然挥之不去——尤其是，你知道的，现在考虑到智能手机的普及，

sentences.en: and like how far we've come from roaming the world or roaming the planes and in tribes, like it doesn't really seem as applicable.
sentences.zh: 以及我们人类离开在平原和荒野中结群游荡的日子已经那么久远了，这种解释似乎没那么适用了。

sentences.en: Like there is another element to this going on.
sentences.zh: 这其中显然还有其他因素在起作用。

sentences.en: Additionally, a fun fact for you, according to the UN,
sentences.zh: 另外，顺便告诉你一个有趣的事实，根据联合国的统计，

sentences.en: 60% of the world lives in densely populated spaces and that would mean
sentences.zh: 世界上有百分之六十的人口居住在人口稠密的地区，这意味着

sentences.en: 60% of people shouldn't be lonely, right?
sentences.zh: 百分之六十的人本不该感到孤独，对吧？

sentences.en: It's very easy to see other people.
sentences.zh: 要见到其他人是非常容易的。

sentences.en: It's very easy to be around them, to feel enmeshed in a tribe.
sentences.zh: 置身于人群中、感受到自己融入某个群体是极其轻而易举的事。

sentences.en: So this idea of just physically being alone, feeling threatening is inaccurate considering that a lot of us aren't physically alone.
sentences.zh: 因此，考虑到我们很多人在物理上并非独自一人，那种仅仅因为身体上孤身一人就感到受到威胁的想法是不准确的。

sentences.en: It is the sense of being emotionally isolated and emotionally unsupported that feels scary.
sentences.zh: 真正让人感到恐惧的是那种在情感上被孤立、在情感上得不到支持的感觉。

sentences.en: And yes, there may be an evolutionary explanation for that.
sentences.zh: 是的，这可能确实有一种进化论上的解释。

sentences.en: It's not the entire thing.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是全部原因。

sentences.en: I think why we shrink from our alone time really comes down to an impending sense that this could be our new normal.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们之所以排斥独处时间，真正归根结底是因为一种迫在眉睫的预感：这可能会变成我们的常态。

sentences.en: And that any further
sentences.zh: 并且任何进一步的

sentences.en: slow escalation of this solitude could leave us entirely isolated before we even realize it.
sentences.zh: 这种独处状态的缓慢升级，都可能在我们甚至还没意识到之前，就把我们彻底孤立起来。

sentences.en: Before we know it, one night in turns into a month of complete isolation and we won't have any say in the matter.
sentences.zh: 不知不觉中，一个晚上的独处就变成了整整一个月完全的与世隔绝，而对此我们毫无置喙的余地。

sentences.en: I don't think it helps that in this day and age we seem to both culturally and socially villainize solitude and loneliness.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在当今这个时代，我们在文化和社会层面上都将独处和孤独妖魔化，这于事无补。

sentences.en: And I think this is for a few reasons as well.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这也是出于以下几个原因。

sentences.en: Firstly, there is the most common but largely fair assumption that people, any person you see who is alone isn't alone by choice.
sentences.zh: 首先，存在着一种最普遍但极其不公正的假设：人们会认为任何一个独处的个人，其独自一人并非出于自愿。

sentences.en: They are alone because nobody wants to spend time with them.
sentences.zh: 他们孤身一人是因为根本没有人愿意花时间陪伴他们。

sentences.en: That is the assumption that we make.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们惯常的假设。

sentences.en: This of course then makes us feel more fearful of being alone ourselves because we think that others will see us at the movies out for dinner and think something is wrong
sentences.zh: 当然，这反过来又让我们对自身的独处感到更加恐惧，因为我们觉得别人会看到我们独自去看电影、独自外出用餐，然后就会觉得我们

sentences.en: with them.
sentences.zh: 有什么毛病，

sentences.en: something has gone wrong in their life or recently.
sentences.zh: 觉得他们的生活最近出了什么差错。

sentences.en: The Society for
sentences.zh: 人格与社会

sentences.en: Personality and Social
sentences.zh: 心理学学会

sentences.en: Psychology actually conducted a study in 2022 on the social costs of seeking solitude and their research showed that others assume that solitude seekers, people who like
sentences.zh: 实际上在2022年进行了一项关于寻求独处之社会成本的研究，他们的研究表明，其他人会假定那些寻求独处的人——也就是喜欢

sentences.en: spending time alone, actually don't care much about belonging to a group.
sentences.zh: 花时间独处的人——其实并不怎么在乎融入某个集体。

sentences.en: They might assume that they're less friendly.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会觉得这些人不那么友好。

sentences.en: Importantly, these negative impressions were often very incorrect but the snap judgment persisted anyways and influenced how people treated those of us who seek solitude.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，这些负面的印象通常是非常不准确的，但这种刻板的第一印象依然存在，并影响着人们对待我们这些寻求独处之人的方式。

sentences.en: A critical way that this happened is that people see others on their own, they believe that these people want to be left alone, that leads to them being left out,
sentences.zh: 这种情况发生的一个关键方式是：当人们看到其他人独自一人时，他们会认为这些人想要独自呆着，从而导致他们被冷落、被排挤，

sentences.en: therefore creating what we think will be a self-reinforcing cycle, one that we don't want to happen to us.
sentences.zh: 因此制造出了我们所认为的自我强化的恶性循环，而这正是我们不希望发生在自己身上的。

sentences.en: You know, we voluntarily spend time alone, soon it's not going to be so voluntary anymore, it's going to be something that happens all the time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们自愿花时间独处，不久之后这就不再那么自愿了，它会变成一件经常发生的事。

sentences.en: The other way that we villainize solitude is through the language that we use to describe people who spend time with themselves and it's not very nice language.
sentences.zh: 我们妖魔化独处的另一种方式是通过我们用来形容那些花时间独处之人的语言，而且这些词汇并不怎么友好。

sentences.en: Think of the phrase, you know, lone wolf to describe somebody who just like suddenly goes and shoots up a school because they're a loner, another word that's not particularly nice.
sentences.zh: 想想“独行侠”这个词吧，它被用来形容那些突然跑去枪击学校的人，因为他们是个孤独的人（loner）——另一个同样算不上多么友好的词。

sentences.en: Women are often branded as like you're a crazy cat lady, you're a spinster if you choose to live alone, particularly if they are romantically unattached, if they spend time by
sentences.zh: 女性常常被贴上这样的标签：如果你选择独自生活，尤其是如果你在感情上没有伴侣、如果你花时间独处，你就会被说成是“疯狂的爱猫老太”、“老处女”，

sentences.en: themselves, as if they are alone because they are undesirable and being undesirable is the worst thing in the world.
sentences.zh: 仿佛她们孤身一人是因为她们毫无吸引力，而毫无吸引力是这世上最糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: All of this language, and that's just three examples, influences our decision to pursue solitude or not because we don't want to be disapproved of, we don't want to be seen
sentences.zh: 所有这些语言——这还只是三个例子——都影响了我们是否要追求独处的决定，因为我们不想遭到社会的非议，我们不希望被同行或其他人用

sentences.en: in a way that is negative by our peers or by other people and that we see other people treated.
sentences.zh: 负面的眼光看待，也不想看到别人受到那样的对待。

sentences.en: Researchers have also argued that solitude has gotten a very bad reputation because we haven't made a deep enough distinction between solitude and loneliness.
sentences.zh: 研究人员还认为，独处之所以名声这么差，是因为我们没有在“独处”和“孤独”之间做出足够深刻的区分。

sentences.en: They are seen as synonymous when they are so different.
sentences.zh: 它们被视为同义词，然而它们截然不同。

sentences.en: We know loneliness has some serious health consequences.
sentences.zh: 我们知道孤独会带来一些严重的健康后果。

sentences.en: It has even been compared to smoking a pack of cigarettes a day in a very famous study.
sentences.zh: 在一项非常著名的研究中，它甚至被拿来与一天吸一包烟相提并论。

sentences.en: We know loneliness just feels awful when we're in it.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道，当我们身处孤独之中时，那种感觉简直糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: It's not something we want to subject ourselves to.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们想要强加给自己的事情。

sentences.en: But solitude doesn't feel the same way and doesn't have the same health impacts.
sentences.zh: 但独处的感觉并不一样，它不会产生同样的健康影响。

sentences.en: You can feel incredibly socially connected and still really enjoy being alone.
sentences.zh: 你可以拥有非常紧密的社会联系，却依然十分享受独自一人的时光。

sentences.en: You can have two, three really good relationships, spend most of your time by yourself, and still not categorize yourself as lonely or experience the health risks that lonely
sentences.zh: 你可以拥有两三个真正的好人际关系，把大部分时间花在自己身上，却依然不会把自己归类为孤独的人，也不会经历孤独者所承受的健康风险。

sentences.zh: 所以，独自花时间相处有点类似于

sentences.zh: 公关危机，

sentences.en: PR problem, I would say, even though, to be honest, we rarely are truly alone anymore.

sentences.en: Texas also found that solitude promotes creativity because it allows for what they call and I love this phrase, the incubation of ideas.
sentences.zh: 也发现，独处之所以能促进创造力，是因为它允许进行他们称之为——我非常喜欢这个词——“想法的孵化”。

sentences.en: Basically, ideas have time to settle, they have time to grow and to develop in isolation from other people before they're kind of out and presented to the world.
sentences.zh: 基本上，想法在与其他人隔离的环境中有了沉淀的时间、生长和发展的时间，然后才被拿出来呈现给世界。

sentences.en: There's a couple of other mental processes they say contribute.
sentences.zh: 他们还指出有其他几个心理过程也在发挥作用。

sentences.en: They talk about this thing called the enhanced ability for the mind to wander, they talk about drifting attention, it all links back to when you are by yourself, some of
sentences.zh: 他们谈到了所谓的心智神游能力的增强，谈到了思绪的漂移，这一切都回归到当你独自一人时，

sentences.en: the walls come down and creative insight is channeled through you.
sentences.zh: 一些心墙会倒塌，创造性的灵感就会通过你流淌出来。

sentences.en: An added bonus to being alone too is that we become much more socially selective.
sentences.zh: 独处的另一个附加好处是，我们在社交上会变得更加挑剔。

sentences.en: When we develop the ability to be happy by ourselves, nobody else can take that from you.
sentences.zh: 当我们培养出独自一人也能快乐的能力时，别人就再也无法夺走这一点。

sentences.en: We really do start to realize like what I previously accepted,
sentences.zh: 我们确实开始意识到，我以前接受的那些对待，

sentences.en: why did I accept that?
sentences.zh: 我当时为什么会接受？

sentences.en: Those people didn't like me, those people weren't nice to me, I don't want to be around those people, I was just afraid of being alone.
sentences.zh: 那些人根本不喜欢我，那些人对一点也不好，我不想和那些人在一起，我当时只是害怕孤独。

sentences.en: And so we're really able to cultivate a deeper sense of self-worth.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们真正能够培养出更深层次的自我价值感。

sentences.en: When solitude stops feeling like a void that you are desperate to fill, I think it becomes a filter instead.
sentences.zh: 当独处不再让人觉得是一个急需填补的空虚时，我认为它反而变成了一种筛选机制。

sentences.en: It becomes a way of testing whether people and certain commitments in your life are actually worth it to you.
sentences.zh: 它成了一种检验你生活中的人和某些承诺是否真的对你有价值的方式。

sentences.en: Because if you've got this great alternative of like
sentences.zh: 因为如果你有了一个很棒的替代方案，比如

sentences.en: I'm going to spend some time by myself and that's amazing, not doing that requires something really special.
sentences.zh: “我要花点时间独自待一会儿，这感觉太棒了”，那么打破这种状态就需要一些非常特别的东西。

sentences.en: And so it means that the things that you let into your life, the standard for them is higher.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你允许进入你生活的事物，其标准会更高。

sentences.en: When being by yourself feels so amazing, I think it just takes a bit more to drag you away from that.
sentences.zh: 当独自一人感觉如此美妙时，我想你需要付出更多的努力才能把你从这种状态中拉开。

sentences.en: And so your life might get smaller but it gets bigger in terms of quality.
sentences.zh: 所以你的生活圈子可能会变小，但在质量上却变得更大了。

sentences.en: The irony is I think our ability to be alone actually creates healthier relationships which people don't always talk about.
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，我认为我们独处的能力实际上创造了更健康的人际关系，而人们并不总是谈论这一点。

sentences.en: When we get better at being solo, we really start to be selective about who we're choosing to join us.
sentences.zh: 当我们更擅长独处时，我们真的开始对选择谁来陪伴我们变得挑剔起来。

sentences.en: Relationships are always a necessity.
sentences.zh: 人际关系并非必需品。

sentences.en: We don't want to be completely hyper independent.
sentences.zh: 我们并不想变得完全极度独立。

sentences.en: But now we're in this state of abundance rather than desperation.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们处于一种丰盛的状态，而不是绝望的状态。

sentences.en: It's like, well, of course I want to have great friendships.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，嗯，我当然想拥有伟大的友谊。

sentences.en: Of course I want to be around people.
sentences.zh: 我当然想和人们在一起。

sentences.en: But I know that I can get that and have that and maybe need less of that than I previously did because my inner well is so deep and because the joy I get from being
sentences.zh: 但我知道我可以得到并拥有这一切，而且可能比以前更不需要这些，因为我的内心源泉如此深厚，因为我从独处中获得的快乐

sentences.en: around myself is so valuable that if somebody isn't going to add to that, I actually don't think I'm going to be pained.
sentences.zh: 是如此宝贵，如果有人不能为之增添价值，其实我并不会感到痛苦。

sentences.en: Whereas previously, if you were somebody like me, it was just like anybody I can get, if that means I don't have to be by myself and I don't have to face a single raw
sentences.zh: 而在此之前，如果你像我一样，那就会变成只要能抓到一个人就行，只要这意味着我不必独自一人，不必直面任何一个

sentences.en: thought, good enough for me.
sentences.zh: 原始的念头，对我来说就足够好了。

sentences.en: You could literally insult me.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以直接侮辱我。

sentences.en: You could literally talk about me behind my back.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以在背后说我坏话。

sentences.en: As long as you were between me and my own feelings and thoughts about something, you were doing a good job.
sentences.zh: 只要你挡在我与自己对某事的真实感受和想法之间，你就做得很好。

sentences.en: This is such a crucial point to be made before I go into how to actually prioritize and enjoy your solitude.
sentences.zh: 在我探讨如何真正优先考虑并享受独处之前，这是一个非常关键的观点。

sentences.en: I will say this is a very critical point that we need to make right here, right now, before we go into how to actually prioritize and enjoy our solitude.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，在我们探讨如何真正优先考虑和享受独处之前，这是一个我们此时此地必须指出的至关重要的观点。

sentences.en: You don't want to go far, too far the other way.
sentences.zh: 你可不想走向另一个极端。

sentences.en: Been there as well.
sentences.zh: 我也曾经历过。

sentences.en: I'm sure some of you have also.
sentences.zh: 我确信你们当中也有人经历过。

sentences.en: You're not meant to constantly be around other people.
sentences.zh: 你并不是注定要时刻和别人在一起的。

sentences.en: You're also not meant to be hyper-independent.
sentences.zh: 你也不是注定要极度独立的。

sentences.en: Sometimes when we get really good at enjoying our own time and space, it molds it and it evolves into this thing where we're only relying on ourselves and we really get this
sentences.zh: 有时，当我们非常擅长享受自己的时间和空间时，它会塑造并演变成这样一种状态：我们只依赖自己，并且真正产生了一种

sentences.en: attitude of like, I don't need anybody.
sentences.zh: “我不需要任何人”的态度。

sentences.en: I don't need help with this.
sentences.zh: “我不需要别人帮忙。”

sentences.en: I can do this by myself.
sentences.zh: “我自己就能搞定。”

sentences.en: Other people are just going to drag me down.
sentences.zh: “其他人只会拖我后腿。”

sentences.en: We're aiming for healthy dependency here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里的目标是健康的依赖。

sentences.en: That is balance.
sentences.zh: 这就是平衡。

sentences.en: Balance is like at the core of human existence.
sentences.zh: 平衡是人类生存的核心。

sentences.en: We are striving for relationships that fill us as deeply as our alone time does and we're striving for relationships where you feel equally, yeah, I guess, fulfilled by
sentences.zh: 我们正在努力维系那些能像独处一样深刻充实我们的人际关系，我们努力追求这样的人际关系：你同样能从

sentences.en: them, but also you find that it gives you good thoughts to go away from that makes your alone time easier because you know that you have the support network and you
sentences.zh: 它们中获得满足感，但同时你也发现它们能带给你美妙的想法，让你在抽离时让独处变得更容易，因为你知道自己拥有支持网络，

sentences.en: have these people who love you and so again there's not this desperation of like, at any point I could be cast out, at any point these people might not like me anymore so I
sentences.zh: 拥有这些爱你的人，所以同样不会产生那种绝望感，即“随时我都会被抛弃，随时这些人可能就不再喜欢我了，

sentences.en: better take what I can get.
sentences.zh: 所以我最好有什么抓什么”。

sentences.en: You lose that feeling and I think both of these interconnected things of connection and solitude become richer together because each is becoming more fulfilling on its own.
sentences.zh: 你摆脱了那种感觉，我认为连接与独处这两个相互关联的事物会因为各自变得越来越充实而共同变得更加丰富。

sentences.en: Hopefully that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 希望这说得通。

sentences.en: So how exactly do we do that?
sentences.zh: 那么我们到底该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: How do we achieve this nice symbiosis?
sentences.zh: 我们如何实现这种美好的共生？

sentences.en: Firstly, we need to work on a fundamental mindset shift which is learning to not fear loneliness or being alone even when it doesn't feel voluntary.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们需要进行根本性的思维转变，即学会不惧怕孤独或独处，即使这种状态并非出于自愿。

sentences.en: Treat your solitude with intention, perhaps even with forced excitement and it will become exciting.
sentences.zh: 带着刻意的心态去对待你的独处，甚至带点强迫性的兴奋去对待它，它就会变得令人兴奋。

sentences.en: If you look at your calendar and it's looking pretty empty, I know the inclination is to panic and fill it.
sentences.zh: 如果你查看自己的日程表，发现空空如也，我知道你的倾向会是恐慌并把它填满。

sentences.en: Instead, I want you to ask yourself like, what does this give me the opportunity to do instead?
sentences.zh: 相反，我希望你问自己：“这反倒给了我什么机会去做别的事？”

sentences.en: What is something that's always just like a little bit better to do by myself anyways?
sentences.zh: 有什么事情无论如何一个人做都要好那么一点点？

sentences.en: What's something that I do when I kind of am like, I probably shouldn't have invited somebody to do this with me.
sentences.zh: 有什么事情是我在做的时候心里会想：‘我刚才真不该邀请别人一起来做这个’？

sentences.en: Do that now.
sentences.zh: 现在就去做这件事。

sentences.en: This is not a punishment.
sentences.zh: 这不是惩罚。

sentences.en: You have not failed.
sentences.zh: 你没有失败。

sentences.en: This is an opportunity and it might sound cliche to label it as such but we know that fundamentally how you experience things begins with how you perceive them.
sentences.zh: 这是一个机会，给它贴上这样的标签听起来可能有些老生常谈，但我们知道，从根本上讲，你如何体验事物始于你如何感知它们。

sentences.en: So targeting that aspect first, targeting perception brings more acceptance and enjoyment further down the line.
sentences.zh: 因此，首先针对这一层面进行调整，针对感知进行调整，会为以后的接受和享受带来更多可能。

sentences.en: If your perception is, I am so excited for this, I am so happy that I get this opportunity, enjoyment will increase.
sentences.zh: 如果你的感知是“我太期待这个了，我太高兴能有这个机会了”，快乐感就会增加。

sentences.en: Something I try and always think of is that you know, at some point in the future, I may have kids and my partner will be sleeping next to me in bed every single night and I'll
sentences.zh: 我试着一直去想的一点是，你知道，在未来的某个时刻，我可能会有孩子，我的伴侣每天晚上都会睡在我身边的床上，

sentences.en: have people needing things from me every hour and I'm most likely not going to have much time to myself.
sentences.zh: 每时每刻都有人需要我帮忙做这做那，我大概不会有多少属于自己的时间了。

sentences.en: In those moments, like when I'm irritated and maybe like a little bit sticky and tired and
sentences.zh: 在那些时刻，比如当我感到烦躁、可能还有点黏糊糊、疲惫

sentences.en: overstimulated, I am going to be thinking back on my
sentences.zh: 且过度受刺激时，我会回想起我

sentences.en: 26-year-old self, Gemma, right now, right here, on how scared she was of spending a night alone, I'm going to beg her to appreciate what she has been missing.
sentences.zh: 26岁的自己，也就是此时此地的杰玛，回想起她当时有多么害怕独自度过一个夜晚，我会恳求她去珍惜她现在所错过的这一切。

sentences.en: I'm going to beg her to be like, just, you don't know what you have, like say in tonight, romanticize the privilege of silence and the privilege of solitude, enjoy this time
sentences.zh: 我会恳求她说：“拜托，你根本不知道自己拥有什么，比如就在今晚留下来，将沉默的特权和独处的特权浪漫化，去享受这段时间的

sentences.en: for what it is.
sentences.zh: 本真意义。”

sentences.en: Whatever you have to say, do, think, believe in, in order to flip that switch in your head, from panic to enjoyment when you have a weekend free or an evening free, do it.
sentences.zh: 无论你需要说些什么、做些什么、想些什么、相信什么，以便在拥有一个闲暇的周末或夜晚时，把脑海中的那个开关从恐慌拨到享受，那就去做吧。

sentences.en: Whatever philosophy you need to believe, believe it.
sentences.zh: 无论你需要相信什么哲学，去相信它吧。

sentences.en: It's also so critical to examine what you're really resisting when you refuse to be by yourself.
sentences.zh: 审视当你拒绝独处时，你到底在抗拒什么，这也是至关重要的。

sentences.en: We speak a lot about this idea that big emotions like fear or anxiety often hide more nuanced secondary emotions that are harder to cope with, like insecurity or instability or
sentences.zh: 我们经常讨论这样一个观点，即恐惧或焦虑等强烈情绪往往隐藏着更微妙、更难以应对的次要情绪，比如不安全感、不稳定感、

sentences.en: emptiness or boredom or existential fatalism, all these things.
sentences.zh: 空虚感、无聊感或存在主义宿命论，所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And I think that our fear of loneliness is a prime example.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们对孤独的恐惧就是一个典型的例子。

sentences.en: I don't really think you're afraid of being bored.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你真的是害怕无聊。

sentences.en: I think you know that you can cope on your own.
sentences.zh: 我认为你知道自己能够独自应付。

sentences.en: I don't think you're afraid of feeling lonely.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你害怕感到孤独。

sentences.en: I think we all know deep down, like you're capable of entertaining yourself.
sentences.zh: 我想我们内心深处都知道，你有能力自娱自乐。

sentences.en: The secondary fear that you are experiencing is, what if I get too comfortable with this?
sentences.zh: 你所经历的次要恐惧是：如果我对这种状态感到太习惯了怎么办？

sentences.en: Or, what if this is a sign of worse to come?
sentences.zh: 或者，如果这是更糟糕的事情即将发生的征兆怎么办？

sentences.en: What if I lose my agency in my own loneliness or solitude?
sentences.zh: 如果我在自己的孤独或独处中失去了自主权怎么办？

sentences.en: I think we treat alone time like it's this diagnostic teSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们对待独处就像是在做某种诊断测试。

sentences.en: A free weekend is not neutral.
sentences.zh: 一个自由的周末并非中性的。

sentences.en: It is evidence that we are becoming these lonely people.
sentences.zh: 它是我们正在变成这种孤独之人的证据。

sentences.en: You know, if we can't fill it, if we're not busy, this is the end.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我们无法填满它，如果我们不够忙，这就是终点。

sentences.en: Like, our mind is building this case, this very fearful, anxious case that, like, I'm never going to find anybody ever again.
sentences.zh: 我们的脑海正在构建这样一种案件，一种非常恐惧、焦虑的案件，仿佛“我再也找不到任何人了”。

sentences.en: Like, my friends are disappearing.
sentences.zh: “我的朋友们都在消失。”

sentences.en: This is, as I said, the beginning of the end for me.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，这对我来说是末日的开始。

sentences.en: Like, I better get out of here.
sentences.zh: 就好像，我最好还是离开这里。

sentences.en: If I don't get invited now, I'm never going to get invited again.
sentences.zh: 如果我现在没被邀请，那我以后就再也不会被邀请了。

sentences.en: The deepest fear is a fear of not just missing out.
sentences.zh: 最深层的恐惧不仅是错失恐惧。

sentences.en: I think it is that fear of never being invited back in and of constant exclusion and not having agency in that.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是永远无法再次被接纳、不断被排挤、并且对此无能为力的恐惧。

sentences.en: And that is very powerful stuff.
sentences.zh: 而这股力量非常强大。

sentences.en: Be aware of that because it's also not reality.
sentences.zh: 意识到这一点，因为它也不是现实。

sentences.en: Not getting an invite one weekend doesn't mean your social life is dead for the rest of your life.
sentences.zh: 有一个周末没收到邀请并不意味着你余生的社交生活就彻底完蛋了。

sentences.en: Another secondary fear that our aversion to alone time is hiding is the fact that when we're alone, we have to confront things that our normally busy, social
sentences.zh: 我们对独处时间的抗拒所掩盖的另一个次要恐惧是，当我们独处时，我们不得不面对那些我们平时忙碌的社交

sentences.en: lives conceal for us.
sentences.zh: 生活为我们掩盖的事情。

sentences.en: All these other things are going to start coming up without the presence of a distraction and not just questions to do with your friends or to do with loneliness, but deeper
sentences.zh: 在没有干扰的情况下，所有这些其他的事情都会开始浮现，不仅是关于你的朋友或孤独的问题，还有更深层的

sentences.en: questions to do with your career and life and purpose and money and trauma.
sentences.zh: 关于你的职业、生活、目标、金钱和创伤的问题。

sentences.en: Being around people constantly means just less of that.
sentences.zh: 经常和人们在一起意味着这种事情会少一些。

sentences.en: It just means that all this stuff that's like really loud feels a little bit quieter.
sentences.zh: 这只是意味着所有这些听起来声音很大的事情会感觉稍微安静一点。

sentences.en: Again, goes to show how much our fear of being alone isn't just a fear of being alone.
sentences.zh: 再次说明，我们对独处的恐惧不仅仅是对孤独的恐惧。

sentences.en: It is wrapped up in
sentences.zh: 它交织在

sentences.en: psychological avoidance and it's wrapped up in a pain point that we just really don't want to push.
sentences.zh: 心理回避之中，并且交织在一个我们真的不想去触碰的痛点里。

sentences.en: I would also like to include here that being alone also includes being comfortable with silence and not filling it with music, not filling it with podcasts.
sentences.zh: 我还想在这里指出，独处也包括习惯安静，而不是用音乐去填满它，不用播客去填满它。

sentences.en: I hate to say it, not filling it with podcasts or audio books or TV.
sentences.zh: 我不愿承认，不用播客、有声书或电视去填满它。

sentences.en: And that is something that I would say all of us are really bad at.
sentences.zh: 而我要说的是，我们所有人在这方面都很差劲。

sentences.en: But in fact, the science has shown is very good for us.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，科学表明这对我们非常有益。

sentences.en: I have been going on and on about this for a hot minute.
sentences.zh: 我喋喋不休地谈论这个已经有一会儿了。

sentences.en: So if you are somebody who knows me personally, please just skip this next part because you've you've heard it over a couple of years at the pub.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你是了解我的人，请直接跳过接下来这部分，因为你在酒吧里已经听过好几年了。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉。

sentences.en: I've been really on my high horse about this, but there is all this research coming out about how the average human will not experience silence ever in their lives.
sentences.zh: 我在这个问题上确实有点好为人师，但现在有大量的研究表明，普通人一生中永远不会体验到安静。

sentences.en: Ever.
sentences.zh: 永远不会。

sentences.en: Unless they like go deaf or something happens, like they are never going to experience silence.
sentences.zh: 除非他们失聪或者发生了什么意外，否则他们永远都不会体验到安静。

sentences.en: And the sad thing is, though, our brains really like silence.
sentences.zh: 但可悲的是，我们的大脑其实非常喜欢安静。

sentences.en: A study from 2006 from the
sentences.zh: 2006年的一项研究来自

sentences.en: University of, I think,
sentences.zh: 我想是

sentences.en: Parvi or somewhere in
sentences.zh: 帕维大学或

sentences.en: Italy revealed how much our bodies do really appreciate it.

sentences.zh: 研究人员在这里划分了一个非常有用的界限：将独处作为一种状态、不合群作为一种人格特质、社交退缩作为一种症状区分开来。

sentences.en: Solitude is temporary and it's voluntary.
sentences.zh: 独处是暂时的，也是自愿的。

sentences.en: You can slip in and out.
sentences.zh: 你可以随时进出这种状态。

sentences.en: You can make choices about it.
sentences.zh: 你可以对此做出选择。

sentences.en: You can enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 你可以享受它。

sentences.en: Unsociability is a preference.
sentences.zh: 不合群则是一种偏好。

sentences.en: You also enjoy it, but it's more of like, you know, you don't always choose it because it's just who you are.
sentences.zh: 你同样享受它，但更像是，你知道的，你并不总是主动选择它，因为它就是你的本性。

sentences.en: You'd very much rather read a book than go to a party even if you're invited.
sentences.zh: 哪怕受邀，你也极其愿意看书而不是去参加派对。

sentences.en: Maybe you'll go, you'll enjoy yourself, but your preference is to be alone.
sentences.zh: 也许你会去，也会玩得很开心，但你的首选还是独处。

sentences.en: Social withdrawal is different.
sentences.zh: 社交退缩则不同。

sentences.en: It's when you are pulling back from people because social interaction feels very threatening or heavy or exhausting, even though that is not typical for you.
sentences.zh: 这是指你开始疏远人群，因为社交互动让你觉得极具威胁、沉重或精疲力竭，尽管这并不是你平日的常态。

sentences.en: And social withdrawal is what we really want to look out for.
sentences.zh: 而社交退缩正是我们需要真正警惕的情况。

sentences.en: In these situations, I think it often indicates
sentences.zh: 在这些情况下，我认为它通常表明

sentences.en: that there has been some experience, some broader pattern in the past, recent past that is pushing you into a space or into a pattern of behavior
sentences.zh: 过去、也就是最近过去曾发生过某些经历、某种更广泛的模式，把你推向了一个空间或一种行为模式中

sentences.en: that you aren't actually comfortable in.
sentences.zh: 而那其实并不是你感到舒服的状态。

sentences.en: I think we see this a lot of time after a bad breakup where you're just like, I just cannot be around people.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在经历糟糕的分手后经常会看到这种情况，当时你就会觉得，我简直无法和别人待在一起。

sentences.en: Or when you're going through grief or a bad friendship situation has left you a little bit traumatized.
sentences.zh: 或者当你经历悲伤，或者一段糟糕的友情让你受到了一点创伤。

sentences.en: You have an innate desire for connection and for more social interaction, but interacting with other people just feels harder than it ever has before.
sentences.zh: 你内心深处仍然渴望建立连接和更多的社交互动，但与他人交往感觉比以往任何时候都更艰难。

sentences.en: You just can't do it.
sentences.zh: 你就是做不到。

sentences.en: You want it, you don't.
sentences.zh: 你既渴望又抗拒。

sentences.en: You want it, you don't.
sentences.zh: 你既渴望又抗拒。

sentences.en: No matter how tricky it feels, we have to remember social skills like most skills can atrophy and kind of break down with disuse.
sentences.zh: 不管它感觉有多棘手，我们必须记住，社交技能就像大多数技能一样，如果长期不用就会退化并逐渐失效。

sentences.en: There's a lot of research suggesting that prolonged isolation can actually make future social interactions feel more and more effortful and more and more anxiety provoking
sentences.zh: 大量研究表明，长期的孤立实际上会让未来的社交互动感觉越来越费力，越来越容易引发焦虑

sentences.en: because we're out of practice.
sentences.zh: 因为我们疏于练习。

sentences.en: And so then that reinforces the need for withdrawal.
sentences.zh: 因此，这反过来又强化了退缩的需要。

sentences.en: It reinforces the fact that we shouldn't be around people.
sentences.zh: 它强化了我们不应该和人群接触的这一事实。

sentences.en: It's called a biosocial psychological feedback loop.
sentences.zh: 这被称为生物社会心理反馈循环。

sentences.en: A lot of fancy words to basically say that when we get into the habit of not being around others because we think that it's scary or hard, the more scary and harder it becomes.
sentences.zh: 用一大堆高大上的词汇，其实也就是在说，当我们习惯了不与他人交往，因为我们觉得这很可怕或很难时，它就会变得更加可怕和困难。

sentences.en: So again, you know beSt.
sentences.zh: 所以话说回来，你知道的，要保持最佳状态。

sentences.en: Sit with it a bit.
sentences.zh: 稍微静心体会一下。

sentences.en: And if you think, you know, I'm just in an independent era and I'm trying to find my balance and I'm just swinging this other way for a little while,
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得，你知道的，我只是处于一个独立期，我正在努力寻找平衡，我只是暂时朝另一个方向偏离了一会儿，

sentences.en: maybe you're all right.
sentences.zh: 也许你一切都好。

sentences.en: But if there's been this gradual avoidance, if there's social anxiety behind this, remember that being around other people is often a lot harder in imagination than reality.
sentences.zh: 但如果这种回避一直在加剧，如果背后存在社交焦虑，请记住，与他人相处在想象中往往比在现实中要难得多。

sentences.en: Remember that there are a lot of people out there who do really like you and really enjoy you and really, really enjoy your company.
sentences.zh: 请记住，外面有很多人其实非常喜欢你、欣赏你，并且真的、真的很喜欢你的陪伴。

sentences.en: No matter what your brain is trying to convince you right now, even if it's 30 minutes with a friend, just make sure you have something on your radar.
sentences.zh: 无论你的大脑现在试图让你相信什么，哪怕只是和朋友相处30分钟，也要确保你的日程里有这样的安排。

sentences.en: Make sure that there is something that you like to do that is social because I want to remind you of that kind of very critical thing we said earlier.
sentences.zh: 确保有一件你喜欢做的、带有社交属性的事情，因为我想提醒你我们刚才提到那个非常关键的观点。

sentences.en: The better you get at spending time alone, the better your relationships should become.
sentences.zh: 你独自相处的能力越强，你的人际关系就应该越好。

sentences.en: And the better your relationships are, the less being alone should feel like a punishment.
sentences.zh: 而你的人际关系越好，独处就越不会感觉像是一种惩罚。

sentences.en: Really, they operate in unison.
sentences.zh: 真的，它们是相辅相成的。

sentences.en: So if you're spending a lot of time alone, but your relationships really aren't improving, something's kind of off balance.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你花了很多时间独处，但你的人际关系并没有真正改善，那就说明有些地方失衡了。

sentences.en: If you're spending a lot of time with other people, but loneliness and alone time starts to feel like this abyss that you can never step towards,
sentences.zh: 如果你花了很多时间与他人相处，但孤独感和独处时间开始变成一个你永远不敢涉足的深渊，

sentences.en: something's also off balance as well.
sentences.zh: 那同样也说明有些地方失衡了。

sentences.en: But that, my friends, is our episode and kind of my guide to how to get better at being alone,
sentences.zh: 但朋友们，这就是本期节目，也是我关于如何更好地独处的指南，

sentences.en: semicolon, without going too far.
sentences.zh: 分号，同时又不过度。

sentences.en: I think the concluding summary headline of this episode is really, if you can control your relationship to solitude, you can control so many of your other reactions.
sentences.zh: 我想本期节目的核心总结标题其实是：如果你能掌控自己与独处的关系，你就能掌控你太多的其他反应。

sentences.en: Loneliness no longer feels like a threat.
sentences.zh: 孤独不再是一种威胁。

sentences.en: It no longer feels like something that is held over your head by bad, unfulfilling relationships.
sentences.zh: 它不再是那种被糟糕、空虚的人际关系悬在你头上的东西。

sentences.en: Doors open because you can go through them alone and reveal more opportunities to do things because you don't need a partner.
sentences.zh: 大门为你敞开，因为你可以独自穿过它们，并由于你不需要伴侣而发掘出更多做事的机会。

sentences.en: You don't need somebody else there to be your companion or to co-regulate you through that.
sentences.zh: 你不需要有另一个人在那里做你的同伴，或者陪你一起度过那种情绪调节。

sentences.en: You may even experience, as we said, greater levels of intelligence, greater levels of creativity, which is very rarely spoken about.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，你甚至可能会体验到更高水平的智力和更高水平的创造力，而这很少被人提及。

sentences.en: Each of us has that set point of time we need to spend around others.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都有一个需要与他人相处的时间基准点。

sentences.en: So respect that need.
sentences.zh: 所以请尊重这种需求。

sentences.en: Respect your introversion, your extroversion.
sentences.zh: 尊重你的内向，尊重你的外向。

sentences.en: Don't entirely deny yourself friendship and connection.
sentences.zh: 不要完全剥夺自己获得友谊和人际连接的权利。

sentences.en: But if you're sitting with a sense of guilt or fear that you don't have as many plans as other people do, that you're wasting your 20s, that you should be busier,
sentences.zh: 但如果你带着一种负罪感或恐惧，觉得自己的计划没有别人那么多，觉得自己在虚度20多岁的年华，觉得你应该更忙碌一些，

sentences.en: I think that this is your permission to let that fear go a little bit and to know that that's actually really, really normal.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是给你的许可，让你稍微放下这种恐惧，并明白这其实非常、非常正常。

sentences.en: And no matter what you see online, people are spending a lot more time by themselves than you think.
sentences.zh: 无论你在网上看到什么，大家花在自己身上的时间其实比你想象的要多得多。

sentences.en: And doing so, opting into that, that's your choice, but you do have a lot to benefit.
sentences.zh: 并且这样做、选择这样做是你的权利，但你确实能从中受益匪浅。

sentences.en: So thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 所以感谢大家的聆听。

sentences.zh: 感谢大家坚持听到最后。
